title: Graceful node evacuation and autoscaler synchronization for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Upgrading Dedicated GPU pools currently relies on naive drain operations that conflict with autoscaler decisions and burst capacity. This causes transient capacity loss for customer tenants during rolling upgrades and can trigger manual intervention. Goal: Implement a coordinated node-evacuation flow and autoscaler handshake that guarantees capacity-safe upgrades for LTS and minor releases without increasing average latency or violating committed throughput for reserved fleets. This ticket covers the orchestration logic, drain APIs, safety gates, and testing harness for Dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New upgrade controller can cordon + evict workload from a node while signaling autoscaler to provision temporary burst capacity when needed
2) Average 99th percentile latency for running requests does not increase more than 10% during a controlled upgrade in staging
3) No dropped requests attributable to capacity starvation during a simulated 20% traffic spike while a 10% subset of nodes are being drained
4) Rollout respects rollout gates (service-level thresholds, canary success criteria) and automatically pauses on SLO regressions
5) Integration tests exercising drain + autoscaler coordination pass in CI and on a dedicated test fleet
tasks: Design drain handshake protocol (cordon -> drain -> eviction -> confirm) and autoscaler API extension
Implement controller: upgrade-controller service changes + retries/backoff
Autoscaler: accept soft-reservation tokens and expose estimated provisioning latency
Update telemetry: add drain events, eviction latency, autoscaler buffer usage metrics
Create chaos test: staged traffic spike during upgrade to validate safety gates
End-to-end tests: simulate multiple tenant workloads and reserved capacity constraints
Documentation: runbook for on-call and Console UI update for visible upgrade progress
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch implementation + unit tests. 2) Deploy controller and autoscaler changes to staging fleet-qa. 3) Run chaos verification harness (3 runs) with controlled traffic spikes; collect SLO metrics. 4) Canary rollout to 5% of Dedicated capacity in us-west with monitoring and automatic pause gates. 5) Expand to 25% then 60% if no regressions; final sweep after 72h of stable metrics. All rollouts must be reversible by controller abort + autoscaler reclaim of temporary capacity.
rollback_plan: If any SLO or error budget threshold breaches the configured gate, the controller will halt further node evacuations, issue a cancel signal to newly provisioned burst nodes, and initiate a rollback operator that reverts nodes to pre-evacuation state (uncordon + ensure cached KV warmup). For persistent capacity shortfall, trigger emergency scale-up of dedicated.burst-pool and notify on-call with runbook reference.
